claims.text: Mansfield testified on 13 May 2026 that unsupported adjustments totalled 'over $859 billion in the last two quarters of FY 25'.
He stated material weaknesses declined from 28 in FY2024 to 26 in FY2025, and that auditors issued 427 fewer Notices of Findings and Recommendations than in prior years.
He stated the Department manages more than $4.7 trillion in assets.
He stated that reporting entities will consolidate from 22 to 7 in FY2027 and that an independent public accounting firm will assume the group auditor role with OIG oversight.

Consolidating 22 separately opined reporting entities into 7 and transferring the group auditor role to a contracted firm both reduce the granularity and the government-held provenance of the annual public audit record. Reasoning: fewer entities means fewer separate opinions published; a contractor group auditor holds the working papers under a commercial engagement rather than as federal records held by an Inspector General.
